q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

items.p: The town's annual kite festival takes place every April on the beach near the old lighthouse. Hundreds of visitors attend each ______ many of them bring homemade kites decorated with bright paper and ribbon.
w: A comma alone between two independent clauses is a comma splice.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
The comma after "and" is incorrect.
items.e: A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses.

items.p: Researchers studying the migration of monarch butterflies have attached tiny, lightweight ______ to the wings of hundreds of the insects so that their routes can be tracked across North America.
w: A comma would separate the verb's object from the rest of the phrase.
A semicolon needs an independent clause on each side.
Nothing that follows explains or lists, so a colon doesn't fit.
items.e: "Tags" is the object of "have attached," and no punctuation belongs between it and "to the wings."

items.p: The architect sketched dozens of designs for the new library before settling on a final ______ the building would have a curved glass front facing the town square.
w: A comma alone creates a comma splice.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
"Which" creates a clause that doesn't fit grammatically with what follows.
items.e: A colon introduces an independent clause that explains what the final plan was.

items.p: The author's most recent novel, ______ was published last fall and quickly became a bestseller in several countries, follows three sisters who run their family's struggling farm.
w: No comma belongs between "which" and its verb.
"It" creates a comma splice inside the sentence.
"And it" leaves the main verb "follows" without a proper subject.
items.e: "Which was published…" is a supplementary clause set off by commas, and "follows" is the main verb.

items.p: Early bicycles had no gears, so riders had to pedal very hard to climb even gentle ______ later designs added gears that made hills far easier to manage.
w: A comma alone between independent clauses is a comma splice.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
The comma after "and" is incorrect.
items.e: A semicolon correctly separates the two independent clauses.

items.p: Opening this weekend at the city museum after two years of planning, the newest exhibit features artifacts from three ancient ______ Egypt, Mesopotamia, and the Indus Valley.
w: A semicolon can't introduce a list.
A comma makes it unclear whether the list names the civilizations.
A period leaves the list as a fragment.
items.e: A colon after a complete clause introduces the list of the three civilizations.

items.p: Marine biologist Lena Okoro—who has studied coral reefs in the Pacific for more than two ______ believes that some reefs may adapt to warmer water faster than scientists once thought.
w: An interruption that opens with a dash must close with a dash.
Without closing punctuation, the interruption runs into the main clause.
A semicolon would separate the subject from its verb "believes."
items.e: The dash pair sets off the supplementary clause about Okoro's research.

items.p: Volunteers removed more than two tons of trash from the river during the spring ______ the city plans to hold a second cleanup in the fall, when water levels are lower.
w: A comma alone between independent clauses is a comma splice.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
The comma belongs before "and," not after it.
items.e: A comma plus "and" correctly joins the two independent clauses.

items.p: The data collected by the weather balloons launched from the coastal ______ helped forecasters predict the storm's path more accurately than ever before, giving residents extra time to prepare.
w: A comma would separate the long subject from its verb "helped."
A semicolon would separate the subject from its verb.
A dash would separate the subject from its verb.
items.e: The subject ("The data… station") must flow directly into the verb "helped," with no punctuation.

items.p: The engineering team's first prototype, built mostly from spare parts, failed during testing in ______ the second, built with a lighter frame, completed every trial without a single problem.
w: A comma before "however" creates a comma splice.
The semicolon must come before "however," since "however" begins the second clause.
Without punctuation before "however," the clauses run together.
items.e: A semicolon ends the first clause, and "however," opens the second.

items.p: The festival's headline performer, ______ a jazz pianist known for blending traditional and modern styles, will close the event on Saturday night with a two-hour concert.
w: Without a comma, the name runs into the description.
A semicolon can't separate these phrases.
A dash can't pair with the comma that opened the phrase.
items.e: The name and the description are each set off by commas as appositives describing "performer."

items.p: To prepare for the two-week mountain expedition, each member of the team packed the same basic ______ a tent, a sleeping bag, a small stove, and enough food for ten days.
w: Without punctuation, the list runs into the clause awkwardly.
A semicolon can't introduce a list.
A comma makes it unclear that the list names the supplies.
items.e: A colon after the complete clause introduces the list of supplies.

items.p: In the 1920s, the city's subway system expanded rapidly, adding new lines to neighborhoods that had previously been reachable only by ______ by 1930, nearly every resident lived within a ten-minute walk of a station.
w: A comma alone creates a comma splice.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
The comma after "and" is incorrect.
items.e: The long first clause ends at "streetcar," and a semicolon joins it to the next independent clause.

items.p: After two years of data collection in schools across the state, the study's conclusion was ______ students who slept at least eight hours performed better on memory tests than those who slept less.
w: A comma alone creates a comma splice.
A semicolon would suggest an unrelated clause, but what follows explains the conclusion.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
items.e: A colon introduces the clause that states what the clear conclusion was.

items.p: Over the past decade, scientists who study ancient ______ have found evidence that some early farmers kept dogs to help guard their herds of sheep and goats.
w: "Who study ancient DNA" is essential, so no comma should separate it from the verb.
A semicolon would separate the subject from its verb.
A dash would separate the subject from its verb.
items.e: The clause "who study ancient DNA" identifies which scientists, so it takes no punctuation.

items.p: The painting, long thought to have been lost during the war, was discovered in an attic in ______ after experts confirmed its authenticity, it was donated to the national gallery.
w: A comma here creates a comma splice.
With no punctuation, the clauses run together.
The comma after "and" is incorrect.
items.e: A semicolon separates two independent clauses; the second begins "after experts confirmed…".

items.p: The chef's signature dish—a soup made from roasted squash, fresh ginger, and ______ has been on the restaurant's menu since it first opened its doors in 2004.
w: An interruption that opens with a dash must close with a dash.
Without closing punctuation, the interruption runs into the main clause.
A semicolon would separate the subject from its verb "has been."
items.e: The dash pair sets off the description of the dish.
